title: Corrosion-Resistant Cabin Floor Seat Track Extrusion for the Galley and Lavatory Runs
abstract: Proposal for a corrosion-resistant seat track extrusion in the wet cabin zones, so that a lease return becomes a cabin refresh instead of a structural job on aircraft that have carried galleys and lavatories for fifteen years.

sections.reason: Every aircraft of this family returning from a first lease has needed seat track work under the forward galley and around the aft lavatories, averaging nineteen metres of replacement per aircraft across eleven redeliveries. The failure is always the same: the anodic layer is consumed by repeated spillage, the track pits along the fastener line and the seat fitting will no longer lock repeatably. The published splice repair is acceptable once at a station but cannot be repeated, so second-lease aircraft are reaching the point where a whole run must be replaced. Barrier sealant applied at cabin refresh delays the onset but does not stop it, because the spillage reaches the track through the fitting slot rather than over the top surface.
sections.description: The extruded track in the wet zones is replaced by a corrosion-resistant alloy section with a sealed fitting slot and a drained lower channel, so that spillage is carried to the existing floor drain path instead of standing in the slot. The clip D5350122405771 is replaced at each floor beam crossing and the upper clip D5350121750926 is renewed, with the vendor plate FAR167574-60 used as the splice at the four positions where a full-length run cannot be shipped. The web NOD599116-78 under the galley hard points is renewed because the new track sits two millimetres higher. Clevis pins LN666073-13 secure the fitting at the monument attachment. The bus bar at FIN 622VC7 runs under the aft floor panel at the aft lavatory station and its support must be re-established after the track is changed. Work is in zones 145, 233 and 263 with the cabin stripped in the affected bays. Detail is on drawing D53501271572.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 26 kilograms per aircraft in a typical two-galley two-lavatory layout, distributed along the cabin floor with a centre of gravity shift below 0.04 per cent MAC. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable: the track height changes by two millimetres, so a modified run cannot be spliced to an unmodified one and the fitting slot geometry differs. The corrosion inspection of the wet zone track moves from a repeat detailed inspection to a general visual at cabin refresh. The floor structure repair task, the parts figure and the wiring sheet for the aft floor all require re-issue, and at least one published splice repair becomes invalid in the modified zones.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Embodiment is a cabin activity of six to nine days depending on the layout, and is intended to be done inside a cabin refresh or at a lease transition rather than as a standalone campaign. No production cut-in is proposed; the affected build standard left the line in 2013.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether aircraft already carrying a splice repair in the wet zones can be modified without removing the splice, whether the two millimetre height change disturbs the galley and lavatory monument attachment interface, how the aft floor wiring support is re-established once the track is changed, and whether the cabin conversion work already published for the aft cabin has effectively done part of this change on some aircraft.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin floor, CG shift below 0.04 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No cut-in; the affected build standard is out of production
